question.text: Amit, an NRI based in Singapore, wants to invest in an Indian AIF. His investment will be governed by:

answer.text: FEMA/NDI rules, the applicable DTAA, and SEBI AIF Regulations
No specific regulations apply to NRIs

explanation.text: The Logic: NRI/PIO investment in SEBI-registered AIFs sits within FEMA's Non-Debt Instruments (NDI) rules and the SEBI AIF Regulations; the applicable DTAA is relevant for Indian tax consequences of offshore-investor returns (pp. 90-95, 260-261). The Trap: "Only Indian tax laws" misses the FEMA/NDI and SEBI dimensions. "Only Singapore regulations" ignores the Indian regulatory framework that governs the investment vehicle. "No specific regulations apply" is plainly incorrect for cross-border investment. Note: Treaty-specific claims (e.g., India-Singapore DTAA articles) or BIPA framing are not directly supported by the cited pages and should be separately sourced before being relied upon.
